examples.answer: popleft takes the oldest cell so we explore level by level; pop would make it a stack, so it goes depth-first and might not find the shortest path.
FIFO means cells closer to the start come out first. With pop() it's LIFO, a DFS, and the first path found could be longer.

examples.answer: BFS explores layer by layer, so all paths of length k come out before k+1. The first time the goal is popped, any shorter path would have been found earlier. This works because every step costs the same.
Cells come out in increasing distance, so the first arrival at the goal is shortest; a shorter path would have reached it first. With weighted edges you'd need Dijkstra.
